problem: The count of distance-1 candidates is wrong by roughly a factor of two. Insertions number 26(L+1) (all letters at L+1 gaps) and substitutions number about 26L, so insertions plus substitutions are about 52L+26, not 26L. The stated total of about 26L + L is far short of the true neighbourhood size.
fix: For a word of length L, distance 1 allows about 26(L+1) insertions, about 26L substitutions, L deletions and L−1 transpositions, roughly 54L edits in all. That is why distance 2 (tens of thousands of strings) needs pruning.

problem: The definition given (one adjacent swap at cost 1, no substring edited twice) is the restricted form often called optimal string alignment; true Damerau–Levenshtein allows repeated edits and the restricted form does not obey the triangle inequality stated just above. A careful reader may think all the metric properties still hold once transposition is added.
fix: Add one sentence: with transposition added, the simple table version that edits no substring twice is the restricted (optimal string alignment) distance, and it can break the triangle inequality; the full Damerau–Levenshtein distance keeps the metric properties.
